questions.prompt: Explain why the volume of the cylinder shown is V = πr²h.
questions.prompt_markup: Explain why the volume of the cylinder shown is V = πr²h.
questions.correct_answer: Each layer is a disk of area πr²; stacking layers to height h gives volume (base area) × (height) = πr²h.
questions.required_method: Think of the cylinder as a stack of thin congruent disks.
questions.grading_note: Any valid explanation. Essential: congruent circular cross-sections of area πr²; volume = base area × height, as for a prism (layers of unit thickness); result πr²h.

questions.prompt: A right cylinder and an oblique cylinder have the same radius r and the same height h. Explain why they have the same volume.
questions.prompt_markup: A right cylinder and an oblique cylinder have the same radius r and the same height h. Explain why they have the same volume.
questions.correct_answer: At every height both cross-sections are disks of area πr², so by Cavalieri's principle their volumes are equal: πr²h.
questions.grading_note: Any valid explanation. Essential: equal heights; equal cross-sectional areas at every level; Cavalieri's principle cited. Invalid: "they look the same size".

questions.prompt: A cylinder has radius r and height h. A square prism has base area πr² and the same height h. Use Cavalieri's principle to explain why the two solids have the same volume, and conclude the cylinder formula.
questions.prompt_markup: A cylinder has radius r and height h. A square prism has base area πr² and the same height h. Use Cavalieri's principle to explain why the two solids have the same volume, and conclude the cylinder formula.
questions.correct_answer: Every horizontal cross-section of the cylinder is a disk of area πr², and every cross-section of the prism has area πr²; equal heights and equal cross-section areas give equal volumes, so V = (πr²)h.
questions.required_method: Compare the cross-section areas at every height.
questions.grading_note: Any valid explanation. Essential: both cross-section areas named and equal at every level; equal heights; Cavalieri's principle; prism volume Bh.

questions.prompt: A cylinder of radius r and height h is approximated by prisms whose bases are regular polygons inscribed in its base circle. Explain why the prism volumes approach πr²h.
questions.prompt_markup: A cylinder of radius r and height h is approximated by prisms whose bases are regular polygons inscribed in its base circle. Explain why the prism volumes approach πr²h.
questions.correct_answer: Each prism has volume (polygon area) × h; as the number of sides grows, the polygon area approaches πr², so the volumes approach πr²h.
questions.required_method: Describe what the polygon base areas approach as the number of sides grows.
questions.grading_note: Any valid explanation. Essential: prism volume Bh; inscribed polygon areas approach the circle area; conclusion.
